description: A Yu-Gi-Oh! card-effect DSL sketch with unfinished Galaxy/Photon and Horus effect-definition scripts.
scope_audience: README frames it as a personal card-authoring layer for an external rules engine, but the host engine and the required symbols are absent from this repository; the intended audience is a rules-engine author.

creativity.reason: The fixed effect-hook tuple plus chainable Cards operations is an interesting local schema for describing card behavior, but no engine or external comparison establishes novelty.

current_usefulness.reason: The scripts can be read as design examples, but they cannot be used as card implementations in isolation and README documents a syntax error.

expected_usefulness.reason: If paired with a compatible host engine, the intended scope could make effect authoring more structured; no integration contract or working consumer is supplied.

impl_progress.reason: script.py contains substantial card-effect data and hook sketches, but its line 90 parse error and absent host symbols prevent an executable slice.

presentability.reason: README clearly labels the project as deprecated and not runnable, with a useful DSL description; it does not provide a self-contained demo.

delivery_likelihood.reason: The target host engine is absent and the principal script has a documented syntax error, so an end-to-end effect cannot be delivered from this repository alone.

verification: README and representative effect data in script.py; executed=false; The documented parser issue and absent globals were assessed statically, not confirmed by running a parser or engine.

evidence.locator: lines 7-45, DSL contract, missing engine and status
lines 1-16, DSL hooks; lines 84-94, effect data and documented parse-error region

contribution: A domain-specific effect-data sketch that makes condition, cost, target and operation stages explicit and pairs them with card text. It is a prototype of an authoring model, not a working card library.
alternatives_question: Which card-effect DSLs or rules engines represent trigger, cost, target and operation stages in data, and how would the same card effect compare in authoring effort and correctness?
reason: The unusual authoring schema and body of effect sketches support a bounded experimental-work route; practical usefulness remains conditional on an absent host engine and repaired syntax.
next_step: Either connect one effect to a compatible engine and validate it against the printed card text, or preserve the repository explicitly as a non-runnable DSL sketch.
